items.title: Mayoral candidates to address food security, housing and income issues at Oct. 1 debate
items.summary: The debate aims to ask mayoral candidates about income, housing and food security. Ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election, Food Banks Mississauga and Metamorphosis Network will host a mayoral debate with the top four polling candidates. Mississauga’s mayoral candidates will be part of a debate on Oct. 1, hosted by Food Banks Mississauga and The Metamorphosis Network. , the food bank’s press release said. The event is being organized to provide candidates with an opportunity to address income, housing security and food availability issues. According to the statement issued by organizers, only the top four polling candidates will be invited to participate. Candidates will be confirmed by Sept. 18. Ahead of the debate, the public is invited to submit questions through an anonymous survey about topics they would like candidates to answer, their policy commitments and goals for their first year in office. Questions can be submitted until Sept. 18. Public registration for the debate opens on Sept.

items.title: Trespassing charge laid after OPP respond to complaint in Mississauga First Nation
items.summary: NEWS RELEASE ONTARIO PROVINCIAL POLICE ************************ An individual has been charged under the Mississauga First Nation Community Protection Law following a trespassing investigation. items.title: 12 townhomes proposed to replace 2 houses in Mississauga
items.summary: A new development proposal would replace two houses with 12 townhomes in Mississauga. , north of the QEW, in Cooksville, according to an application submitted to the City of Mississauga. Two homes are on the properties, which would be demolished, along with any sheds or other structures, to make way for the development. Much of the mature vegetation will also be removed, but the developer hopes to keep the trees along the rear and side lot lines. The proposed townhomes will be located within two blocks that will flank a common element condominium roadway. Access to the property will be from Harborn Road. Five units will be in a block on the west side of the private road and seven units will be in a block on the east side. All of the townhomes will have private driveways and single-car garages accessed from the common element roadway. There will be sufficient space on the individual driveways to park a vehicle. Additionally, four visitor parking spaces, including one accessible space, will be located at the south end of the roadway.

items.title: 100-kilometre trail will link Mississauga, Brampton and other Ontario communities
items.summary: A 100-kilometre trail that when completed will run from Mississauga’s Lake Ontario shoreline through Brampton to north of the Greater Toronto Area recently hit another milestone as the decades-long project approaches the halfway mark. A new 40-metre pedestrian bridge was officially opened last week along the developing Credit Valley Trail at the Upper Credit Conservation Area in Caledon. Credit Valley Conservation, which owns the property, called the new bridge “a major new infrastructure project that will help connect the trail from the Credit River headwaters in Orangeville to Port Credit at Lake Ontario” in Mississauga. ” CVC is the organization that protects natural areas and watercourses in Peel’s three municipalities and several other communities including Orangeville, other places in Dufferin County and Halton Hills. “This new pedestrian bridge marks an important step forward in bringing the vision of the Credit Valley Trail to life,” said Terri Hamilton, CVC chief administrative officer. “By connecting the trail across the Credit River, this vital link makes it easier for people to experience the natural beauty of the Credit River Valley while strengthening connections between communities. ” The major initiative to build the 100-kilometre Credit Valley Trail began nearly a decade ago and it’s scheduled to be completed in 2041, according to the conservation authority. The trail, currently at 43 kilometres, is “taking shape,” CVC said earlier this year. “Once complete, the Credit Valley Trail will be a 100-kilometre trail from Dufferin County to the Mississauga shoreline.

items.title: Man injured in stabbing overnight in Mississauga
items.summary: A man was injured in a stabbing early Thursday morning in Mississauga. com. Police believe the stab wound was sustained during an altercation that occurred sometime overnight in the area of Cawthra Road and Lakeshore Road East in Lakeview. The 33-year-old man suffered a non-life-threatening stab wound, police said. Police said he was transported to a local hospital by ambulance for treatment. Investigators are currently working to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and how the injury was sustained. At this time, there is no information to suggest an ongoing threat to public safety, police added. Police did not provide suspect information.

items.title: Mississauga Falls in National Happiness Rankings as Brampton Surges to Near the Top
items.summary: According to INsauga, a new Leger survey measuring happiness in Canada's 10 largest cities found Brampton posting one of the biggest year-over-year jumps in the country while Mississauga's ranking slipped. The outlet reports Brampton rose to second place among the 10 cities this year, up from fifth in 2025, tied to a five-point increase in resident happiness scores. INsauga reports the increase is the largest year-over-year jump recorded among the ten largest cities in the survey. According to the outlet, Mississauga's showing looked very different, with the city dropping several spots to land in sixth place this year. The outlet notes the shift highlights a growing divide in resident sentiment between the two neighbouring Peel Region cities, even as they share many of the same regional economic and social pressures. INsauga reports Leger's annual survey has tracked happiness levels across Canada's largest cities for several years, offering a rough gauge of how residents feel about life in their community.
